title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory audit that tested conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact normalized equality, fuzzy 5-gram overlap, provenance heuristics) and a guarded exclusion policy on a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample. The preregistration targeted four public OpenAlex benchmark identifiers, but the executed confirmatory sample used provenance-stable synthetic tasks produced by a deterministic task generator and the pipeline reused a single shared generation per item (shared_initial_candidate semantics). These two recorded execution facts rendered the primary paired estimand (guarded minus baseline validator pass rate) degenerate: all 150 baseline and matched guarded episodes passed the deterministic validator (baseline = 150/150, guarded = 150/150), giving a paired difference = 0.0 percentage points (95% CI [0.0,0.0]) and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Crucially, this numeric null is artifact-supported but uninformative about contamination prevalence in web-sourced public benchmarks because (1) the confirmatory sample provenance was synthetic (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and (2) independent re-generation per condition was disabled (execution/model_configuration.json). We reconcile preregistration→execution differences with concrete archived artifact references (paths recorded below), explain why per-item fuzzy-overlap summaries are absent (detector persistence policy recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json), and give artifact-grounded recommendations (provenance-rich sampling, independent_condition_generation=true, full per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication) to make future audits sensitive to public-corpus contamination.

sections.introduction:
LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated configuration repair. Operational trust in such systems requires that benchmarked accuracy reflects model competence rather than dataset contamination (items or templated prompts appearing in model training data) or narrow templated constructs. Meta-analyses and recent surveys therefore recommend contamination-aware evaluations that combine deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance checks, and verifier-backed oracles.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered a confirmatory audit to answer: under conservative deterministic contamination detectors and a guarded exclusion policy, how many high-confidence flags arise in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample, and how much does applying those controls change a single hosted LLM's validator pass rate? Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered experiment (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) executed end-to-end and archived; (2) artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces; and (3) an explicit preregistration→execution reconciliation that documents why the run produced a degenerate null and prescribes artifact-anchored design changes to increase audit sensitivity.

Scope and bounded claims. The preregistration explicitly listed four public OpenAlex benchmarks as the intended sampling pool: https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W4404602270, https://openalex.org/W4404534210, and https://openalex.org/W7166900660. The executed confirmatory sample instead used provenance-stable synthetic tasks produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The execution also set independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in execution/model_configuration.json. Because these execution facts are recorded in the archived artifacts, the observed zero-flag, zero-difference outcome applies only to this synthetic, shared-generation regime and does not imply absence of contamination in independent public benchmarks.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and verification. Prior systems and benchmark studies show LLMs can synthesize plausible configuration artifacts and propose repairs; integrating deterministic verifiers or iterative validate–repair loops improves average repair quality relative to naive generation. Formal tools such as Header Space Analysis and localized subspecification provide practical oracles for reachability and policy checks and are commonly embedded in generate–validate pipelines.

Evaluation validity and contamination. Surveys and methodological critiques highlight two evaluation threats: contamination (benchmark items leaking into model training data) and construct invalidity (benchmarks dominated by templated or low-complexity items). Recommended defenses include deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, timestamp/provenance checks, and explicit reporting of detector outputs. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses under a preregistered analysis plan and demonstrates how execution choices (sampling provenance and generation semantics) determine audit sensitivity.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We preregistered study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1 and froze: detector definitions and thresholds, guarded exclusion/replacement rules, sampling plan (task_count = 150), generation semantics as a tunable parameter, verifier rules, and the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The planned analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1 using an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Sampling and generation semantics. The preregistration allowed either public-item sampling or deterministic synthetic generation. The executed run used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce 150 synthetic tasks; per-item generator seeds and the source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:" are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (artifact path: execution/task_manifest.jsonl; the execution manifest records its SHA-256). The executed model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) set independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics), which caused the pipeline to perform a single model generation per item and reuse the shared candidate for both baseline and guarded episodes unless a high-confidence exclusion triggered a replacement. This behavior reduced actual hosted model calls (model_calls_used = 150) relative to the preregistered maximum of 300 and mechanically collapses baseline vs guarded discordance when no exclusions occur; counts and provider-call accounting are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.

Contamination detectors and guarded policy. The preregistered detector suite implemented three deterministic heuristics: (1) exact normalized token equality (exact match → high confidence); (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence threshold ≥ 0.80 (sensitivity thresholds at 0.65 and 0.50 for secondary analyses); and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics comparing item timestamps/DOIs to public-archive cutoffs. The guarded policy excluded only high-confidence flagged items (exact match or 5-gram ≥ 0.80) and replaced them deterministically via retemplating/topology augmentation from the same task generator; replacements required an embedding-similarity safeguard (cosine ≥ 0.85). The detector implementation persisted detailed per-item fuzzy overlap outputs only when thresholds were crossed or replacements invoked; this detector persistence policy is recorded in the transformation manifest (execution/transformation_manifest.json). Because no items met the preregistered high-confidence criteria in this run, no replacements or flagged-event persistence occurred and the archive contains an empty analysis/contamination_summary.csv rather than a global overlap table.

Verifier and scoring. The deterministic oracle deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) parsed candidate configurations, simulated state updates, and checked task-specified final-state and workflow constraints. The scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation requires final modeled state parity on allowed fields and respect for workflow constraints (sequence, protected interfaces, group constraints). The validator emits binary pass/fail and per-episode traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes); these traces are archived for every episode (execution/scoring/*.json).

Analysis plan and accounting. The registered primary test is the single paired McNemar test on the 150 item pairs. Secondary sensitivity analyses were preregistered (treating failed calls as failures; fuzzy-threshold sensitivity; subgroup analyses by templated vs realistic). The execution adhered to the missingness and retry policies (one automated retry; none needed). All seeds, provider traces, raw responses, and validator traces were archived (see execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis artifacts). Exact artifact paths are: execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/contamination_summary.csv (the execution manifest records full SHA-256 values for these artifacts; see execution/execution_manifest.json for recorded hashes).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. The run completed planned_episode_count = 300 episodes (150 item pairs): completed_episode_count = 300, failed_episode_count = 0. Because independent_condition_generation = false and no high-confidence exclusions occurred, the pipeline used model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item) rather than two separate generations per condition; the deterministic_reconciliation artifact and execution/execution_manifest.json record these counts and provider-call accounting.

Contamination detector outcomes. The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags in the executed sample. analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged rows; the detector workflow persisted no threshold-crossing logs because none occurred (detector persistence policy recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json). Consequently no replacements were performed.

Validator outcomes and primary statistics. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (archived in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. All raw model responses and validator traces that substantiate these counts are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json).

Representative diagnostic. A representative episode (pair-000001 / task-000001) shows identical normalized reference and response strings and validator traces with parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 4 and score = VALID_CONFIGURATION; that episode and others are present in the execution bundle (examples under execution/scoring/).
sections.discussion:
Why the primary test is degenerate and uninformative for public-benchmark contamination. The numeric null (0.0 difference, p = 1.0) is artifact-supported but uninformative about contamination in independent public datasets because two executed choices recorded in the archive systematically removed the conditions under which the guarded policy could alter outputs: (1) synthetic provenance: the confirmatory sample was drawn from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and each task manifest entry contains source_identifier entries prefixed with "synthetic-netops:" (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl); and (2) shared generation semantics: execution/model_configuration.json set independent_condition_generation = false so the pipeline reused a single shared model output per item for both baseline and guarded episodes when no exclusion occurred. Together these facts mechanically collapse baseline/guarded discordance and reduce model_calls_used to 150, leaving the paired estimand untestable for generation-level leakage. The execution artifacts explicitly record both facts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/model_configuration.json) and provider-call reconciliation (execution/execution_manifest.json and deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Absence of per-item fuzzy-overlap summaries. The detector implementation persisted detailed fuzzy-overlap outputs only when thresholds were crossed or replacements invoked; this persistence policy is recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json. Because no high-confidence flags occurred, no global per-item overlap table was emitted in the archive (analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty). This absence is an explicit consequence of the archived detector configuration and not an omission of logging; it reduces post-hoc interpretability about how close items were to the 0.80 threshold and motivates changing the detector persistence policy to always persist per-item scores in future runs.

Design changes to increase audit sensitivity (artifact-grounded). The recorded execution artifacts show concrete, implementable adjustments that would make future audits sensitive to contamination in web-sourced benchmarks: (A) sample provenance-rich public items (the preregistration already listed OpenAlex targets but execution used synthetic items); (B) set independent_condition_generation = true to generate independent baseline and guarded outputs per item (this flag is recorded and was false in execution/model_configuration.json); (C) persist full per-item fuzzy 5-gram overlap scores to analysis/contamination_scores.csv regardless of threshold crossings (the current transformation manifest documents the alternate persistence rule); (D) expand to multiple models and independent seeds (increase model_calls_used and complete_pair_count) to raise expected discordance and statistical power; (E) add paraphrase-robust detectors and human adjudication for borderline fuzzy cases. Each recommendation follows directly from gaps visible in the current archived outputs: model_calls_used = 150, an empty contamination_summary.csv, and lack of a per-item overlap artifact.

Operational implications. The archived validator traces confirm that, under the tested synthetic tasks and allowed-state constraints, LLM-generated configurations can satisfy task-level functional constraints as checked by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. However, passing a task-specific validator does not imply production readiness or absence of semantic regression beyond the validator's modeled properties. Auditors and practitioners should therefore combine provenance-rich sampling, independent generation, cross-model checks, and human adjudication when assessing operational contamination risk and model reliability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-for-NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence contamination flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The null outcome is artifact-supported and stems from provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared-generation semantics; it does not imply absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks. We provide an explicit preregistration→execution reconciliation, confirm deterministic reconciliation checks passed, and recommend artifact-grounded changes (provenance-rich sampling, independent generation, persistent per-item overlap logging, multi-model scope, and paraphrase-sensitive checks) to increase audit sensitivity in future runs. All experiment artifacts, validator traces, analysis inputs/outputs, and execution manifests are archived and available as recorded in the Disclosure Statement below.

limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

Sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") for this run; absence of high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance or human adjudication.

Passing the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
